messages.author: efb064044f1e1c0f
messages.subject: t.test and summarising multiple columns
parts:
I´m trying to summarise multiple columns getting a mean, sd and a p-value using a t-test. 

data(mtcars)
library(dplyr)
mtcars%>% summarise_each(funs(mean=mean(.,na.rm=T),sd=sd(.,na.rm=T),t_p=t.test(.~vs,data=.)$p.value), vars = disp:qsec)

I did post at StackOverflow (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/26244321/dplyr-summarise-multiple-columns-using-t-test) but no-one was able to figure out how to use a t.test with a formula. Any ideas?

Best,
M

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: t.test and summarising multiple columns
parts:
Hi:

Here are a couple of approaches using both plyr and tidyr.

(1) Write a function that returns a data frame of the means, SDs and
p-value for the t-test of each numeric variable by vs and then call it
with do().

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Base data frame with which to work. It is a molten data frame
# with the categorical/count variables cyl, am, gear and carb removed
# gather() is akin to reshape2::melt()

DFm <- mtcars %>% select(mpg, disp:vs) %>% gather("var", "val", -vs)

## Function to apply to each data split
f <- function(DF)
{
pv <- t.test(val ~ vs, data = DF)[["p.value"]]
means <- tapply(DF$val, DF$vs, mean)
sds <- tapply(DF$val, DF$vs, sd)
stats <- c(means, sds, pv)
names(stats) <- c("mean0", "mean1", "sd0", "sd1", "p.value")
data.frame(as.list(stats))
}

# Apply it through the pipeline
DFm %>% group_by(var) %>% do(f(.))


## (2) Pure dplyr/tidyr approach

# Start by computing the data frame of summary stats
# by variable (rows) and vs (cols) - akin to reshape2::dcast()
DFstats <- DFm %>%
group_by(var, vs) %>%
summarise_each(funs(mean, sd), val) %>%
gather(stat, statval, mean, sd) %>%
unite(stat_vs, stat, vs) %>%
spread(stat_vs, statval)

# Tack on the p-values from the t-tests
cbind(DFstats, DFm %>%
group_by(var) %>%
do(data.frame(pval = t.test(val ~ vs, data = .)[["p.value"]])))

Dennis

messages.author: efb064044f1e1c0f
messages.subject: Re: t.test and summarising multiple columns
parts:
I did something similar to Dennis and ended up with:

mult_t.test<-function(df,by_var,...){
  require(dplyr)
  require(tidyr)
  by_var<-deparse(substitute(by_var))
  j<-df%>%gather(var,val,...)
  t<-j%>%group_by(var)%>%do(v=tes(.,by_var))
  k<-data.frame(levels(t$var),matrix(unlist(t$v),ncol=3,byrow = T))
  names(k)<-c("var",names(t$v[[1]]))
  k
}


tes<-function(df,vart){
  x<-t.test(df$val~df[[vart]])
  p<-x$estimate
  p<-c(p,p.val=x$p.value)
  p

}
